dedupe_keys.name: i 24 motion freeway vehicle trajectory data interstate 24 nashville

description: I-24 MOTION (Interstate-24 MObility Technology Interstate Observation Network) is a traffic observation instrument near Nashville, Tennessee, described by Derek Gloudemans, Daniel B. Work and co-authors. Its 276 pole-mounted high-resolution cameras cover about 4.2 miles of a four to five lane freeway with frequent congestion; video is sent over fibre to a compute facility where computer vision extracts the trajectory of every vehicle, with its dimensions and class. About 230 million vehicle miles are travelled through the section each year. Coverage: the first public datasets contain at least four hours of trajectories on each of ten days; the team states that all trajectory data will be released at i24motion.org/data as the system matures. Format and access: trajectory datasets described in the 2023 arXiv paper. Licence and cost: free to download per the paper; no licence could be read because the website did not respond on 2026-09-29. Caveats: one freeway section only; extraction errors from computer vision are possible. The data support calibration of car-following and lane-changing models, capacity and congestion-wave analysis on freeways. It relates to the NGSIM, highD and INTERACTION trajectory datasets in the catalogue.
